source.publisher: USDA Forest Service Forest Inventory and Analysis
source.negativeEvidencePolicy: Missing FIA detections support research status only. They never support verified absence or survey non-detection.

partition.wallTimeQualification: The crash-recovered command stream did not retain one durable end-to-end partition timer. No synthetic throughput rate is reported.

workerCanaries.qualification: The accepted worker rate covers local replay of an already acquired national archive. It is not a network acquisition or national certification forecast.

disk.reason: The measured free-space margin above the five-worker threshold was too small and APFS capacity was volatile.

throughput.qualification: Acquisition, local partition, worker replay, integration, compilation, and production QA are distinct workloads. The centralized partition lacked one durable timer, so no end-to-end automated-source forecast is claimed.

manualInterventions: Replaced two full worker worktrees with sparse worktrees after measuring disk use.
Preserved one Alaska partial result because retired county codes could not be mapped to active county equivalents under the approved geography policy.
Corrected the projection validator to filter immutable reviews to the same bounded species scope as assertions.
Expanded bounded acquisition projection scope with immutable outcome species so reviewed source results for unknown state-species decisions are not silently excluded.

forecast.qualification: No national certification date is defensible from the current measurements. The worker replay point estimate excludes acquisition, state-specific research, blocked geography, freshness review, integration, and production QA.

knownContradictions: The prior projection exposed only 2,451 of the new FIA explicit outcome pairs because source-targeted species whose state applicability remained unknown were filtered out of bounded projection materialization. The corrected sparse model retains unknown applicability while publishing the reviewed source outcomes.
The resource policy nominally permits five lightweight workers above 8 GiB free, but measured capacity was too close to that threshold for a safe five-worker wave.
The Alaska canary produced valid reviewed evidence but remained partial because retired county codes cannot be assigned to active county equivalents without an approved crosswalk.
